body: City Council - Study Session and Regular Meeting
agenda_text:
AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL - STUDY SESSION AND REGULAR MEETING
  NOVEMBER 5, 2019
REGULAR MEETING
  6:15 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Margarita L. Rios, Mayor
  Luigi Vernola, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Leonard Shryock, Councilmember
 Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
 the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
 subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
 minutes.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
 certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
 matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
 meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
 devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
 documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
 Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
 that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
 has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
 during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
 telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

  Pastor Joe Jenkins

  1.  CERT Highlights

  2.  Halloween Parade Recap
   3.  Halloween Festival Recap

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of October
  15, 2019. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period September 22 –
  October 5, 2019, in the total amount of $929,057.51. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  October 9 – October 29, 2019, in the total amount of $2,551,037.49. 640

  Warrant Register

  4.  CLAIM AGAINST THE CITY - Staff recommends City Council deny the claim filed by Geico (Cuevas).
  830-03

  Report

  5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – OCTOBER 23, 2019 - No action is required unless the City
  Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the
  Commission’s action was final. 320

  Report

  6.  ORDINANCE NO. 19-1708 – Staff recommends City Council accept for second reading and adopt
  Ordinance No. 19-1708, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AMENDING NORWALK
  MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 15.32 ADDING LANGUAGE REGARDING A NEW CODE
  COMPLIANCE APPEAL FEE AND MODIFYING THE FILING DATE FOR APPEALS TO CITY
  COUNCIL. 305-03/602-01

  Report

  7.  CONFIRM EMERGENCY WORK – REPLACEMENT OF EXISTING HEATING, VENTILATION AND
  AIR CONDITIONING (HVAC) UNIT AT CITY HALL, ROOM 15 - Staff recommends City Council confirm
  emergency replacement HVAC work completed by Tri-West Mechanical, Inc., in the amount of $7,750.
  955

  Report

  8.  RESOLUTION NO. 19-68 – APPROVING THE CITY’S APPLICATION FOR GRANT FUNDS FOR THE
  2019 ENVIRONMENTAL ENHANCEMENT AND MITIGATION (EEM) PROGRAM - Staff recommends
  City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-68, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK APPROVING THE APPLICATION FOR ENVIRONMENTAL ENHANCEMENT AND
  MITIGATION (EEM) PROGRAM. 623

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  9.  ADVISORY BODIES - Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200
   Report

ORDINANCE AND RESOLUTIONS

  10. ORDINANCE NO. 19-1709 – ADOPTING BY REFERENCE THE 2019 CALIFORNIA BUILDING,
  RESIDENTIAL, FIRE, PLUMBING, ELECTRICAL, MECHANICAL, EXISTING BUILDING, AND
  GREEN BUILDING STANDARDS CODES AND AMENDMENTS – RESOLUTION NO. 19-70 –
  MODIFYING THE CALIFORNIA STANDARD CODES DUE TO LOCAL CLIMATIC, GEOLOGICAL OR
  TOPOGRAPHICAL CONDITIONS – AMENDING THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE – Staff
  recommends City Council:

  a.  introduce for first reading by title only Ordinance No. 19-1709, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK ADOPTING BY REFERENCE THE 2019 EDITIONS OF THE CALIFORNIA
  BUILDING, RESIDENTIAL, FIRE, PLUMBING, ELECTRICAL, MECHANICAL, EXISTING
  BUILDING, AND GREEN BUILDING STANDARDS CODES AND RELATED MODEL CODES,
  WITH APPENDICES AND AMENDMENTS THERETO; AND AMENDING THE NORWALK
  MUNICIPAL CODE, and waive further reading;

  b.  adopt Resolution No. 19-70, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK MAKING EXPRESS FINDINGS AND DETERMINATIONS THAT MODIFICATIONS TO
  THE CALIFORNIA BUILDING, RESIDENTIAL, FIRE, PLUMBING, ELECTRICAL, MECHANICAL,
  EXISTING BUILDING, AND GREEN BUILDING STANDARDS CODES IN ORDINANCE NO. 19-
  1709 ARE REASONABLY NECESSARY BECAUSE OF LOCAL CLIMATIC, GEOLOGICAL OR
  TOPOGRAPHICAL CONDITIONS; and

  c.  set a public hearing date for December 3, 2019. 305-01

  Report

  11. RESOLUTION NO. 19-69 - AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2019/20
  ADOPTED BUDGET FOR UNION PACIFIC RAILROAD (UPRR) PRELIMINARY ENGINEERING
  PLAN REVIEW OF PROJECT NO. 7196 - FIRESTONE WIDENING - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 19-69, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 ADOPTED
  BUDGET FOR UNION PACIFIC RAILROAD PRELIMINARY ENGINEERING PLAN REVIEW OF
  PROJECT NO. 7196 – FIRESTONE WIDENING, in the amount of $75,000; and

  b.  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and amendments provided there is funding
  in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1005-04-7196

  Report

  12. RESOLUTION NO. 19-71 - AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 ADOPTED BUDGET TO
  ACCEPT THE NATIONAL RECREATION AND PARK ASSOCIATION’S 10-MINUTE WALK PLANNING
  GRANT AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AWARD - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 19-71, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK, CALIFORNIA AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2019/20
  ADOPTED BUDGET ACCEPTING AND ADDING THE NATIONAL RECREATION AND PARK
  ASSOCIATION’S 10-MINUTE WALK PLANNING GRANT AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE
  AWARD, in the amount of $40,000; and

  b.  authorize the City Manager to execute any agreements or documentation required by the grant, on
  behalf of the City, in forms approved by the City Attorney. 420-03/610

  Report

  13. RESOLUTION NO. 19-72 – AUTHORIZING APPLICATION FOR AND RECEIPT OF SENATE BILL 2
  PLANNING GRANTS PROGRAM FUNDS PROMOTING HOUSING DEVELOPMENT – Staff
  recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-72, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING APPLICATION FOR, AND RECEIPT OF, SENATE BILL 2
  PLANNING GRANTS PROGRAM FUNDS AND AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER OR
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR TO EXECUTE THE AGREEMENT AND ANY
   AMENDMENTS. 623

  Report

  14. RESOLUTION NO. 19-73 - CONSIDERATION OF ADDING A REVENUE IMPROVEMENT MEASURE
  TO THE CITY’S MARCH 3, 2020 GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION – Staff recommends City Council
  adopt Resolution No. 19-73, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK,
  CALIFORNIA APPROVING AND ORDERING THE SUBMISSION TO THE QUALIFIED ELECTORS
  OF THE CITY AT THE MARCH 3, 2020 GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION A PROPOSED
  ORDINANCE AMENDING CHAPTER 3.30 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE TO IMPOSE
  A .75% TRANSACTIONS AND USE TAX TO BE ADMINISTERED BY THE CALIFORNIA
  DEPARTMENT OF TAX AND FEE ADMINISTRATION. 845-03

  Report

REPORTS

  15. AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 6 - PERFORMANCE UPDATE TO METROLINK CIVIC CENTER
  SHUTTLE PROGRAM – RESOLUTION NO. 19-74 - BUDGET AMENDMENT – Staff recommends City
  Council:

  a.  authorize the City Manager to execute Amendment No. 6 with MV Transportation, Inc. in the
  amount of $137,390 to extend the Pilot Shuttle Program from December 1, 2019 through June 30,
  2020 on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney; and

  b.  adopt Resolution No. 19-74, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2019/20 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE PROPOSITION C FUNDS TO SUPPORT A PILOT SHUTTLE
  SERVICE, in the amount of $137,390. 1120-05-02

  Report

  16. AGREEMENT – LEGAL SERVICES - Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement with
  Alvarez-Glasman & Colvin to serve as the City’s Attorney for a term of three years effective October 15,
  2019, with an option to extend for two additional years upon written confirmation at the rates specified
  in Exhibit A of the agreement. 815-01

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated October 31, 2019.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
